subject: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthcore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear signal on HealthCore's production goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so we have alignment before we draft SLA language.

Call highlights (agreed high-level):
- Target workflow: real-time transcription + clinical note generation for telehealth sessions.
- Peak concurrency observed on call: target support for 300 concurrent sessions; expected sustained concurrency 120-150.
- Latency targets you requested: 1) streaming first-byte p50 <= 150ms, 2) streaming tail p95 <= 500ms for a 2–3 minute session, 3) non-streaming generation p95 <= 800ms.
- Throughput: average token emission ~ 40–60 tokens/sec per session during active streaming; peak bursts up to ~120 tokens/sec.

Open questions we flagged on the call (need your preference so we can finalize measurement definitions):
1) Measurement start/end: do you want Redwood to measure latency from (A) request arrival at Redwood ingress or (B) request receipt at HealthCore edge LB?
2) Streaming measurement semantics: does HealthCore want first-byte and continuous per-token latency included in the SLO, or only per-session tail metrics?
3) Exclusions: we'd expect mobile network spikes, scheduled maintenance windows, and declared DDoS attacks to be excluded — please confirm any additional exclusions (e.g., third-party transcode services).
4) Remedies: do you prefer a service-credit based remedy or a fixed percentage billing credit? Any financial cap we should be aware of?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll produce an SLO matrix (attached) that shows candidate thresholds, measurement windows (1m/5m/1h), and suggested exclusions.
- Marissa will draft specific SLA language covering measurement points and reporting cadence for your legal review.
- If you prefer measuring from your edge, we can provide a light-weight probe (signed URL) and instructions for a passive span to correlate timestamps.

Attachments: hc_slo_matrix.xlsx (candidate thresholds), redwood_streaming_playbook_v1.pdf (how we measure streaming), SLA_draft_healthcore_v1.docx (initial wording — DRAFT).

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 11/23: Redwood sends draft SLA & SLO matrix (Marissa).
- Wed 11/25: HealthCore legal/procurement confirms exclusions + remedy preference.
- Week of 11/30: finalize SLA and circulate for signatures / DocuSign.

Can you confirm the measurement start point preference (ingress vs your edge) and whether you want first-byte included as part of the streaming SLO?

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

--
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthcore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies

Aditya — thanks for the crisp recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

Measurement point: HealthCore prefers measurement from our edge (we want to own the client-to-edge network variability as part of our product-level SLO). That said, we need Redwood's server-side metrics to be authoritative for root cause / remedy calculations.

Streaming semantics: we want both first-byte and tail included in the SLO set. First-byte p50 is important for perceived responsiveness; tail p95 we view as our reliability SLO.

Exclusions: agree on mobile network spikes and force majeure. Please add third-party ASR/transcoding provider outages to the exclusions list — we will flag those in incident reports.

Remedies: procurement prefers service credits tied to monthly invoice with a cap equal to 25% of monthly contract value. We'll require a table of credit tiers by severity.

We'll review the attachments and get back to legal/procurement next week. For the measurement-from-edge option, can Redwood provide the passive-span guidance and a signed URL test you mentioned?

Emily Zhao
Senior Director, Platform Engineering | HealthCore
emily.zhao@healthcore.com

--
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthcore.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies

Thanks Emily — noted on measuring from HealthCore's edge for perceived client latency and keeping Redwood metrics as authoritative for service processing time. I attached a short SLA language excerpt in SLA_draft_healthcore_v1.docx that does two things:

- Defines two latency dimensions for streaming: first-byte latency (server processing + network to first byte) and tail latency (time to final token). Each has its own target and reporting window.
- Defines measurement boundaries:
  * If measuring from HealthCore edge, the contract will require timestamp correlation via a signed probe; Redwood will accept HealthCore-provided spans as record-of-occurrence for most incidents, but Redwood reserves final adjudication rights if spans are incomplete.

Suggested remedies table (excerpt):
- Severity 1 (monthly availability < 99.5%): 10% invoice credit
- Severity 2 (p95 latency breaches > 3 occurrences/month): 5% invoice credit
- Cap: 25% of monthly contract value (matches procurement ask)

Open engineering clarification for Rishi: around token-rate bursts — HealthCore told us they can see up to 120 tokens/sec in spikes. We need to confirm whether those bursts are short-lived (<10s) or sustained (>=60s) to size concurrency and buffer settings.

Action items:
- Aditya: capture HealthCore preference on burst duration (Emily) so Rishi can map to autoscaling policy.
- Rishi: will draft a short appendix on burst handling and recommended buffer/backpressure behavior and share by Tue 11/24.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthcore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies

Emily — quick follow-up: are the 120 tokens/sec bursts you mentioned observed for periods closer to 5–15 seconds (short bursts) or longer than 60 seconds (sustained)? That will materially change the autoscaling/burst capacity we recommend.

Also, procurement asked for a sample credit table and a one-line definition for what constitutes a breach event vs. a transitory spike. Marissa has a draft in the SLA doc, but procurement wants it explicit in a separate one-pager.

Thanks,
Aditya

--
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthcore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap: streaming & concurrency qualification — measurement, exclusions, remedies

Aditya / team —

Quick answers: most bursts are short (5–20s) during speaker transitions; sustained bursts >60s are rare but we have seen them during system tests. We'll confirm a small sample trace set for Rishi to analyze.

Procurement also asked that the remedies table include an explicit exclusion for any downtime caused by customer-configured webhooks or integrations (we will mark those in postmortems).

We can sync legal/procurement with Redwood on Thu 11/26 at 10:00am ET — please confirm if that works for your team and send a calendar invite.

Emily
